task.title: VSCode extension YOLO mode - read Claude settings and pass --dangerously-skip-permissions flag
task.description: Add support for Claude's YOLO mode (bypass permissions) in the VSCode extension. When users have YOLO mode enabled in Claude's settings, the extension should automatically pass the --dangerously-skip-permissions flag when creating terminal instances to run kanban commands.
task.problem: Users who have YOLO mode enabled in Claude's settings (via .claude/settings.json or ~/.claude/settings.json) still get prompted for permissions when using the kanban extension. The extension creates terminals and runs `claude "/kanban-..."` commands, but doesn't pass the --dangerously-skip-permissions flag even when the user has configured Claude for bypass permissions mode.
task.value: Seamless workflow for users who've opted into YOLO mode. By respecting Claude's existing permission settings, users don't have to approve every tool call - the extension matches their expected Claude behavior. This removes friction from the kanban workflow and respects user preferences already configured in Claude's settings.
task.acceptance-criteria:
Given the extension is activated And the user has Claude settings configured When the extension reads .claude/settings.json or ~/.claude/settings.json Then it should detect if "dangerously-skip-permissions": true OR "defaultMode": "bypassPermissions" is set
Given YOLO mode is detected in Claude settings When the extension creates a terminal to run a kanban command Then the command should be invoked as `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions "/kanban-..."`
Given YOLO mode is NOT detected in Claude settings When the extension creates a terminal to run a kanban command Then the command should be invoked as `claude "/kanban-..."` (current behavior)
Given both project-level (.claude/settings.json) and global (~/.claude/settings.json) settings exist When reading settings Then project-level settings should take precedence over global settings
